name: CO-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Denver-based district with a D+29 partisan lean makes a Democratic hold near-certain
Melat Kiros raised over $1.1 million versus roughly $2,000 for Christy Peterson
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at about 99 percent
Open seat and third-party candidates on the ballot could trim the Democratic margin
model.rationale: The district's D+29 lean, Kiros's overwhelming fundraising advantage, and markets pricing a Democratic win near certainty leave no plausible Republican path; only the size of the margin is genuinely in question.
model.watch: Consolidation of independent and Libertarian support, or depressed Democratic turnout in a low-salience open-seat race, could narrow the margin without changing the likely winner.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Diana DeGette (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Denver's CO-01 is one of the most Democratic House districts in the country, with a partisan lean of D+29, and longtime incumbent Diana DeGette is not on the ballot after losing renomination. Democratic nominee Melat Kiros enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised over $1 million and drawn both supporting and opposing outside spending. Republican Christy Peterson has raised roughly two thousand dollars, leaving little sign of a competitive Republican operation. Polymarket prices a Democratic win at about 99 percent.

An independent, Shimon Blau, has raised a modest sum, and Libertarian and other candidates also appear on the ballot, which could shave a few points off the Democratic margin in a low-salience race. Even so, the district's fundamentals make a Republican victory implausible; the realistic question is the size of the Democratic win.
